output.myth: Every house on the Spindle has a smoke-hole, and every smoke-hole has a rule. The smoke goes up straight from the hearth, the way a good line goes up from a reel, and climbs past the gulls. Then it stops. It stops at a height no one has reached, like washing that forgot to dry. Hesk, who keeps count at the pole, saw it the first time and said nothing. Aun, who cut the string, looked up and asked what was waiting there. The old women say the smoke is waiting for someone to come home. Aun flew a sealskin kite up to find out. The smoke did not move for him, and he did not come down the same. So when you light the fire at dusk, bank it low and keep the pot on. Mend your nets while it burns.
output.verse:
Smoke climbs from the hearth,
It climbs past the gulls, then stops.
Keep the hearth; come home.
